title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
one_liner: 让研究 Agent 重写其搜索与上下文管理代码，以固定预算下的留出任务表现选代，并单独检验后续自我改进能力。

problem.text: AI 可以优化研究任务代码，但负责搜索的 Agent 自身能否以相同预算获得更好的研究效率？AIDE²把研究 Agent 的代码作为优化对象，尝试让它自己改搜索策略、记忆与验证流程。本文为 Weco AI 2026 年 9 月的预印本。

gap.text: 下游任务得分上涨既可能来自更多算力，也可能来自对选择题集的过拟合，不能直接证明研究过程更好。更强的 RSI 主张还要求改进后的系统更擅长继续改进系统。本文分别检查固定预算、外部任务泛化和这项更强的 ignition test。

method.text: 内层 Agent 在任务预算内搜索代码，观察公开信号并返回一个解；系统在隐藏数据评分后跨任务平均，得到 Agent 的私有等级。外层根据历史 Agent 与等级重写当前版本，保留最高分版本。主循环中底座固定：外层 Claude Opus 4.7，内层 Gemini 3 Flash；外层选择规则本身也是固定的。

trace.text: AIDE0 倾向不断改最高分节点，并把全部日志放入上下文。演化后的 AIDE85 使用策略臂上的 bandit 选择、周期性分叉、短上下文摘要和由错误率触发的失败记忆。它改变的是如何分配同一任务预算，而不是直接提高底座模型参数。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入为 AIDE0 代码、人工开发的外层 AIDEhuman、机器学习/算法/Agent 工程选择任务和预算；输出为被评估的源码候选及版本谱系。每个候选必须重新执行内层任务，最终另用 ALE、MLE、FML 与基于 WeatherBench 2 的任务测试迁移。

results.text: 主运行 8 天、99 次重写提案，接受 7 次改进，私有等级由 0.703 到 0.778。外部评估中 AIDE85 相比 AIDE0：ALE 1536→1790，MLE 私有百分位 0.678→0.722，FML 平均归一化提升 15.0%→19.9%；不同 benchmark 指标不能相加。ALE 为 10 题×10 种子，MLE 为 22 题×3 种子，FML 为 18 题×3 种子，各组内部预算相同。

contributions.text: 把研究效率自身变成可选择的改进目标，并把选择集上的改进与外部任务泛化分开。还在未参与选择的内核任务上观测奖励投机下降。尤其提出 ignition test：比较发现出的 Agent 和发现它的 Agent 谁更能驱动下一轮改进，而不是由下游分数直接推定。

limitations.text: ignition test 每组只有 3 个 50 步运行，最终均值约 0.780 与 0.782，作者认为不足以区分自我改进效率。因此不能声称已验证持续加速。两层噪声和昂贵复评限制统计把握；源码越来越复杂，仍不清楚哪些组件真正贡献收益。

cost.text: 主自修改运行耗时 8 天，论文未在这些设置中给出一个统一总美元成本。外部测试 ALE/MLE 每任务 5 美元，天气任务 15 美元；FML 则以 100 步为主约束。天气与 FML 使用不同底座，不能误写成全部外部测试共用 Gemini 3 Flash。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：近期 RSI 代表性实证，适合先读方法和 ignition test。它直接指出演化后 Agent 难解释的实际问题，但没有用机制解释驱动自改；可与审计工具对照理解“性能改善”和“理解改善”之间的证据缺口。

均为嵌套元优化；AIDE²强化固定预算、隐藏评分和外部 benchmark 泛化。

classification_reason: 主循环由固定外层改进内层；另以 ignition test 将演化后的 AIDE47 部署为外层改进器。三种子结果不足以确定改进效率优势，专项检验不等于主循环已持续自加速。

en.one_liner: AIDE² rewrites a research agent’s search and context-management code, selects versions using held-out performance at a fixed budget, and separately tests whether the evolved agent can drive further improvement.

sections.problem: Can the agent running a research search become more efficient at the same budget? AIDE² makes the research agent’s own code the optimization target, allowing changes to its search strategy, memory and validation workflow. This card covers Weco AI’s September 2026 preprint.
sections.gap: A higher task score can come from extra compute or overfitting to the selection tasks. A stronger claim also requires the evolved system to become better at producing further improvements. The paper therefore examines fixed-budget performance, transfer to external tasks and a separate ignition test.
sections.method: An inner agent searches over task code, observes public feedback and returns a solution. Hidden-data scores are averaged across tasks to give the agent a private rating. An outer agent rewrites the current version using previous agents and their ratings, retaining the highest-scoring version. The main loop keeps Claude Opus 4.7 as the outer model, Gemini 3 Flash as the inner model, and the outer selection rule fixed.
sections.trace: AIDE0 repeatedly edits its best-scoring node and keeps all logs in context. The evolved AIDE85 instead uses bandit selection across strategy arms, periodic branching, short context summaries and failure memory triggered by error rates. These changes redistribute the task budget. They do not update the underlying model’s weights.
sections.inputs_outputs: The inputs are AIDE0’s code, the human-developed outer agent AIDEhuman, selection tasks in machine learning, algorithms and agent engineering, and a budget. The outputs are evaluated source-code candidates and their lineage. Each candidate must rerun the inner tasks. Transfer is then tested on ALE, MLE, FML and tasks based on WeatherBench 2.
sections.results: The main run lasted 8 days and made 99 rewrite proposals, accepting 7 improvements. Its private rating rose from 0.703 to 0.778. On external tests, AIDE85 versus AIDE0 scored 1790 versus 1536 on ALE, 0.722 versus 0.678 in MLE private percentile, and 19.9% versus 15.0% in FML mean normalized improvement. These are different metrics. ALE used 10 tasks × 10 seeds, MLE 22 × 3, and FML 18 × 3, with equal budgets within each comparison.
sections.contributions: The work makes research efficiency a target for selection and distinguishes selection-set gains from transfer. It also observes less reward exploitation on kernel tasks excluded from selection. Its ignition test asks whether the discovered agent can drive subsequent improvement more effectively than the agent that discovered it.
sections.limitations: The ignition test has only three 50-step runs per group. Final means of about 0.780 and 0.782 were insufficient, in the authors’ assessment, to distinguish self-improvement efficiency. The evidence therefore does not establish sustained acceleration. Noise at both levels and expensive reevaluation limit statistical power, while growing code complexity makes component contributions hard to isolate.
sections.cost: The main self-modification run took 8 days, with no single total dollar cost reported for these settings. External ALE and MLE tests allowed $5 per task, weather tasks $15, and FML mainly used a 100-step constraint. Weather and FML tests used different underlying models, so the external evaluations did not all use Gemini 3 Flash.
sections.relevance: Library analysis. This is a recent empirical RSI study worth reading for its method and ignition test. It exposes practical difficulty in explaining evolved agents, but it does not use mechanistic explanations to drive self-modification. It helps separate evidence of better performance from evidence of better understanding.

related.darwin-godel-machine: DGM uses coding ability as a proxy. AIDE² directly selects research-task optimization efficiency and separately tests whether the discovered agent can drive further improvement.
related.stop: Both use nested meta-optimization. AIDE² emphasizes fixed budgets, hidden scoring and generalization to external benchmarks.
